newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr developing a range-bound mentality.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr developing a range-bound mentality.

text.p: The Australian dollar remained heavy at the midsession as loose talk on the prospects of a domestic rate cut kept the market on edge and indecisive.

Dealers said U.S. banks were on the offer after a New York investment house sold in size overnight, but were meeting Asian and exporter bids at US$0.7740. There was talk an Asian name was protecting a strangle options position, although such rumours often reflected a range-bound mentality rather than reality.
There had been real signs of Japanese demand for government bonds and A$ buying related to dual currency samurai bonds with another issue of 15 bln yen reportedly launched Wednesday.
By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the currency was loitering at US$0.7748/53 from an early US$0.7760/65 and US$0.7777/82 late here Wednesday, with the day's range so far a miserly 8 ticks.

It had now spent more than a week bouncing around in a broad US$0.7690/7795 band and looked set to remain there short term as the local market squared up for the ANZAC Day holiday tomorrow and a raft of domestic econmic data next week.
A break of US$0.7680 or US$0.7820 was needed to break the deadlock and, given large stops were building either side, could easily see a 1/2 cent lunge afterwards.
On the crosses the currency followed the U.S. dollar in easing back on the mark to 1.3268/80 having leapt to more than a pfennig to 1.3320/37 late Wednesday.

It was a shade off at 97.77/87 yen from 97.92/02 but underpinned by speculation of further yen/A$ dual currency samurai bonds. NSW TCorp launched the first issue in a while Tuesday and dealers believed a 15 bln yen issue for the Asian Development Bank had been launched by Daiwa on Wednesday.
Domestic data on motor vehicle registrations showed a 1.3 percent rise in March confounding forececasts of a 2.25 percent fall and continuing a strong run. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
